profile.headline: Software Engineer at Facebook
profile.summary: Experienced Full Stack Developer with a passion for interesting data and impactful technology. Skilled in Python, Java, Web Development, and Leadership. Strong educated professional graduated from University of California, Merced.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Software Engineer with 6+ years of experience at Meta building large-scale platform infrastructure. I specialize in distributed systems reliability, security architecture, and developer experience — turning complex multi-quarter migrations into production-ready systems that serve thousands of engineers. My work spans serverless architecture migrations (80% latency reduction, 139K compute-hours saved annually), multi-tenant credential isolation systems (2M+ daily workloads secured), distributed queue re-architecture, and SLO frameworks that cut incident detection time from hours to minutes. I've mentored multiple engineers from onboarding to independent ownership, and led cross-team initiatives spanning 50+ teams. Currently focused on AI-powered operational investigation agents — combining deep infrastructure expertise with LLM capabilities to automate production diagnostics at scale.

Core skills: Python, C++, Erlang/OTP, serverless, container orchestration, distributed systems, SRE, platform engineering, developer tooling, security & privacy engineering.

positions.title: Rotational Software Engineer
positions.description:
WhatsApp Group Chat Backend Infrastructure | Erlang/OTP, Distributed Systems

As a Rotational Software Engineer at Meta, I worked on WhatsApp's Group Chat backend infrastructure — a distributed Erlang/OTP system serving billions of users. I contributed to core backend operations including group chat management, participant handling, and identity model refactoring, systematically migrating endpoints from raw identifiers to typed actor-based identity wrappers across dozens of interdependent modules.
This role gave me deep hands-on experience with distributed systems at massive scale: storage layer operations, real-time messaging protocols, and building for reliability in a system where downtime is measured in user-minutes across billions. It also shaped my long-term focus on platform infrastructure, developer experience, and production resilience.

positions.title: Lead Instructor
positions.description: Teaching Web Design through Amazon Web Services' Lightsail and WordPress. I help teach the web design class where students from various ages, experiences, and backgrounds come together to learn about web sites and how create and modify one. We follow a basic curriculum consisting of up to 10 lessons after which we help the students meet the specific needs of their websites. Whether it be additional CSS, Search Engine Optimization, or implementing Amazon Associate features, we equip the students to find solutions they need through the basic tools we teach them.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Build a web app for users to sign up to test pre-release products.

positions.title: Java Developer
positions.description: Maintain and Enhance UI Applications at the front end and back end levels. Take lead and ownership on projects and codebases related to UI Applications. Create and maintain features for handling vendor payments and card authorization controls. Worked in Java, Spring, Oracle, and either JSP or Angular on some projects.

positions.title: Peer Tutor
positions.description:
Computer Science and Engineering tutor for PALS (Peer Assisted Learning Support) with the Bright Success Center at UC Merced.

I tutored students from all backgrounds in all introductory CSE Classes. I related experience that the students have to concepts in their CSE classes to help them relate to the material better. In one semester, I even tutored a Python class I never took, just based off of my side experience in Python.

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
UC Merced School of Engineering, Merced, CA                                                                             May 2016 – August 2016
Research Assistant
I reported to one of UC Merced’s founding CSE faculty, Shawn Newsam. During my time as a researcher, I created models using Tensorflow to detect pets in images obtained from Flickr, collaborated with another student to parse georeferenced metadata of images taken in San Francisco, and helped design maps in ArcGIS showing hotspots where images of each type of pet were taken to determine pet activity in each region.

We found many interesting results, such as the fact that dog pictures are mostly taken at parks and tourist attractions such as Embarcadero, and the fact that cat pictures are mostly taken indoors at home.

The data we found could be useful to any entity planning to open a pet shop in San Francisco.

Our team won first place in the Undergraduate Student division of research presentations.
